headline: Keredo is a clipping of けれども (keredomo, “although, but”), first attested in 1711.
Saru's ultimate derivation is possibly borrowed from Ainu サロ (saro, “monkey”).
Takamaru is 高 (taka, root of 高い, “high, tall”) plus -maru, developed from Classical Japanese 高む.
Sayū is 左 (sa, “left”) plus 右 (yū, “right”).
Uketoru is 受ける (ukeru, “to receive”) plus 取る (toru, “to take”).
Nezumi was originally 根 (ne, “root”, signifying somewhere hidden away) plus 住み (sumi, “to live”): “one who lives in hidden places”.
Kuu went from kupu through kuwu to kuu; the medial w vanishes but resurfaces in kuwanai and kuwareru.
Joō is Middle Chinese 女王, literally “female + king”.
Jōkyō is Middle Chinese 上 (MC dzyangX) plus 京 (MC kjaeng).
Minoru is usually considered 実 (mi, “fruit”) plus 乗る (noru, “to ride”), though noru may be a corruption of なる (naru, “to bear fruit”).
テニス is borrowed from English “tennis”.
億, “hundred million”, is a Middle Chinese borrowing (MC 'ik).
ベテラン is the English word “veteran” in katakana.
こんな is a contraction of この様な (kono yō na).
エプロン is borrowed from English “apron”.
逆, “reverse, opposite”, is a Middle Chinese borrowing (MC ngjaek).
シャッター is borrowed from English “shutter”.
流れる comes from the classical lower bigrade verb 流る (nagaru).
ペン is borrowed from Dutch “pen”.
ボーナス is borrowed from English “bonus”.
苦しい is analysed as a compound of ⟨kuru-⟩, which indicates stress or temper, and the adjectivizing suffix ⟨-si⟩.
ウール is borrowed from English “wool”.
かなり is 可 (ka, “acceptable”) plus なり (nari, “to be”, archaic).
エチケット comes from French “étiquette”.
氏, “family name, lineage”, is a Middle Chinese borrowing (MC dzyeX).
ダイヤグラム is the English word “diagram” in katakana.
オイル is the English word “oil” in katakana.
解ける descends from the classical 下二段 verb 解く (toku).
レコード is borrowed from English “record”.
ふわふわ is imitative; the source compares English “fluffy” and Hungarian “puha”.
スクリーン is borrowed from English “screen”.
